title: Prom and Semester
premise: Ines Voss has spent three years holding her family together with color-coded schedules and careful silences, so when her best friend Marisol disappears the night before prom, leaving only her car keys and a torn note on Ines's porch, Ines is the one everyone expects to fix it. Following the keys leads her and Marisol's ex, Theo, into a cover-up involving Marisol's uncle's smuggling operation — a truth Marisol fled to escape rather than endanger the people she loves. As the semester's end forces every secret into the open, Ines must choose between protecting Marisol's silence and telling the police what she knows, even though it may cost her the friendship and expose her own family's fragility. The truth comes out at the prom Marisol never got to attend; Marisol is found alive, testifies, and Ines learns that love that survives the truth is the only kind worth keeping.
about_author: Quentin Nakamura is a former night-shift paramedic who writes young adult fiction about kids who grow up too fast. They live in a coastal town much like the one in this book, where the fog always seems to be keeping a secret.

chapters.title: The Careful Life
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. We meet the Voss household in its precise choreography: mom leaving for the night shift, Ines managing homework, dinner, and her siblings' schedules. The emotional beat is exhausted devotion — Ines has built a life so controlled that the reader can feel the pressure about to break it.

chapters.title: Prom Court and Other Lies
chapters.summary: Ines's POV at school. Marisol is voted prom committee chair and giddily plans a night Ines can't afford to attend; Theo, Marisol's ex, lingers with unfinished business. The beat is warm friendship shadowed by class tension and a first hint that Marisol is hiding something behind her brightness.

chapters.title: Keys on the Porch
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Marisol misses their Friday ritual; at dawn Ines finds Marisol's car keys and a torn note reading 'if they ask, I was never —' on the porch. Panic, guilt, and the terrible knowledge that Ines was the last person Marisol trusted. Beat: the careful life shatters.

chapters.title: Everyone Looks at the Responsible One
chapters.summary: Ines's POV under police questioning. Detectives fixate on Ines because she 'knows everyone's business.' Meanwhile her siblings sense her unraveling. Beat: the weight of being the reliable one — everyone assumes Ines can carry this too, and no one asks if she's drowning.

chapters.title: The Ex Who Won't Leave
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo admits he and Marisol argued days before she vanished — about her uncle Ray's 'warehouse job' she'd been helping with. He shows Ines a text Marisol sent: 'I know what's in the boxes.' Reluctant alliance forms. Beat: suspicion curdling into shared fear.

chapters.title: What the Keys Open
chapters.summary: Ines and Theo, alternating POV. The keys fit Marisol's car — and a storage unit. Inside: cash, burner phones, and a ledger with names, including, guttingly, Ines's own mother. Beat: the discovery that the danger is woven through everyone Ines loves.

chapters.title: Mom's Night Shift
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, home. Ines confronts her mother, who confesses she took 'off-book' cash from Ray Vargas to cover rent during the year dad left — not knowing what it funded. Beat: Ines realizes her mother's sacrifice and Marisol's silence are the same disease: love that hides the truth to protect people.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours of Almost
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo and Ines retrace Marisol's last week: a fight at the marina, a burned receipt, a witness who saw Ray's truck near the cliffs. The siblings nearly fall apart at home when Ines misses a shift. Beat: the investigation and the family both fraying at once.

chapters.title: The Note's Other Half
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines finds the torn half of Marisol's note tucked in her yearbook — 'I was never brave enough to tell you.' It reframes everything: Marisol ran to protect Ines, not from her. Beat: grief turning into resolve; Ines stops being careful and starts being dangerous.

chapters.title: Ray Vargas Buys Dinner
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ray appears at the Voss door with groceries and sympathy, offering to 'help find Marisol' while probing what Ines knows. A masterclass in menace disguised as kindness. Beat: Ines must smile and lie — loyalty and truth pulling in opposite directions for the first time in the story.

chapters.title: What Theo Did
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confesses he once took money from Ray to pay for Marisol's college fund, which is why Marisol broke up with him — and why he's terrified he caused her flight. Beat: guilt, honesty, and the fragile trust between Ines and Theo hardening into something more.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Missing Page
chapters.summary: Ines and Theo, alternating POV. They decode the ledger: Ray is moving contraband through the marina, and the missing page names the buyer — someone connected to the school board. Beat: the conspiracy is bigger and closer than they imagined; prom itself is the drop night.

chapters.title: Little Witnesses
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines's youngest sibling innocently reveals they saw Marisol's car at the marina the night she vanished. Ines realizes Marisol may not have run — she may have been taken or hidden nearby. Beat: hope with teeth; the search narrows.

chapters.title: Telling the Truth Costs
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines gives the detectives the ledger, knowing it exposes her mother. Mom is questioned; the household cracks; her siblings blame Ines. Beat: the theme made flesh — truth as an act of love that still wounds everyone it touches.

chapters.title: Prom, Without Her
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Prom night: Ray's drop is happening under the gym's noise and glitter. Ines and Theo attend not to dance but to watch, wired with fear. Beat: the novel's central irony staged — the celebration of youth as the site of its greatest danger.

chapters.title: The Drop
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, climax part one. Ines follows the buyer to the marina during prom, calls the police, and is caught by Ray. He reveals Marisol is alive, hidden at the old cannery, kept quiet to guarantee his crew's silence. Beat: terror and relief fused — the stakes become a countdown.

chapters.title: The Cannery
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, climax part two. Theo creates a diversion; Ines finds Marisol locked in the cannery office, weak but alive. Ray corners them; sirens close in; Marisol chooses, at last, to speak the truth aloud to Ray's face. Beat: courage as the thing Marisol fled to find.

chapters.title: After the Sirens
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ray is arrested; Marisol is hospitalized; the ledger implicates and then, through cooperation, protects Ines's mother. Marisol won't see Ines — ashamed of every lie. Beat: the hollow aftermath of victory; truth saved a life and broke a friendship.

chapters.title: Semester's End
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV (first appearance since chapter 2's framing). Marisol narrates her reasons: the uncle she loved, the friend she couldn't bear to endanger. She watches Ines from across the schoolyard, unable to cross it. Beat: empathy for the one who hid; the cost made personal.

chapters.title: What Ines Couldn't Say
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Final exams, final sibling chaos, mom working a day shift now that the truth is public. Ines writes Marisol a letter she doesn't send, then decides to say it to her face instead. Beat: Ines chooses honesty over safety one last time — this time for the friendship.

chapters.title: The Conversation at the Marina
chapters.summary: Ines and Marisol, alternating POV, one scene. At the marina where it began, they trade every truth: the lies, the fear, the money, the love. It is not easy and not instant, but Marisol says 'you told the truth even though it cost you' — and means it as thanks. Beat: reconciliation earned, not gifted.

chapters.title: Prom and Semester
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, epilogue. Summer: the school throws Marisol the prom she missed — a gym full of paper stars, Theo and Ines dancing badly, Marisol laughing for the first time in chapters. Ines lets her siblings see her cry. Beat: the careful life replaced by an honest one; love that survived the truth.
